title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.
source: Meetup Yolo County Board Game Gathering

title: Grounded Together: Building Resilience, Connection, and Community
description:
Iama Embodied Community
***P.S. this is part of a 5 week series, though not required, you are highly encouraged to attend all - No meeting on Oct 7***

Join **Rev. Rola Al-Ashkar** for a five-week journey exploring how our life experiences shape the way we respond to stress, conflict, belonging, and relationships. Through storytelling, guided reflection, and gentle body-centered (somatic) practices, participants will develop tools for greater self-awareness, emotional resilience, and compassionate listening.
Whether you're seeking personal growth, healthier relationships, or a deeper sense of connection within our community, this series offers a welcoming and supportive space. No prior experience is necessary. Please register using the following link: [[LINK](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdxWVImvnFcRLw5on8gH2WFGQfoMnVmNowpxZd9FHajblr2Iw/viewform?usp=send_form)].
**Wednesdays:** Sept. 16, 23, 30; Oct. 14 & 21 6:00 – 8:00 pm

title: National Disability Employment Awareness Month 2026
location: CA
description:
Since the 1970s, National Disability Employment Awareness Month (NDEAM) has taken place every October. NDEAM reinforces the message across the U.S. that people with disabilities provide invaluable roles and perspectives to our diverse American workforce. 
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports that one in four adults (at least 60 million) in the U.S. live with a disability. This statistic is based on what is reported, however. So, it’s possible that the number is higher than what is stated.

title: UC Davis Multicutural Calendar - October
location: CA
description: The Multicultural Calendar is a valuable tool for enhancing understanding, and respect for religious and cultural observances.  It serves as a resource for students, staff, and faculty to plan events, activities, meetings, retreats, and courses throughout the year. title: Free Yoga Practice
description:
Iama Embodied Community
🌀 **Move with intention. Connect with your body. Celebrate community.**

Join us every **Thursday at 6 PM** for an embodied yoga practice designed to help you release tension, ground yourself, and cultivate presence. This is a trauma-informed, all-levels class, no prior yoga experience needed. Expect a Hatha-Vinyasa flow, breathwork, and a space to listen to your body’s wisdom.

🌿 **Every last Thursday of the month, stay after class for a community potluck dinner!**

📍 **Location**: 727 T St. Sacramento CA 95811
✨ **All our events are free. Donations are welcome.**
📩 **Questions? Reach out at** embody.iama@gmail.com
🔗 **Follow us on Instagram:** [@embody.iama](https://www.instagram.com/embody.iama)

title: DJUSD Board Meetings
location: City Hall Community Chambers, 23 Russell Blvd, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
DJUSD Board meetings offer insight on how the school district remains responsive to the community’s values, beliefs, and priorities. The Board meetings occur on every first and third Thursday, in the City of Davis Community Chambers. 23 Russell Boulevard. Public session starts at 6:30 PM.  Meetings are cablecast live on Channel 17 (Comcast) or streamed on the DJUSD-TV website. 
  
The Davis Joint Unified School District’s Board of Education is comprised of five community members, responsible for setting district policy, approving the budget, and hiring the superintendent for schools in Davis, California. The agendas for the meetings are posted at least 72 hours in advance. 
  
For more information on special meetings, agendas, public comment, and more, visit the DJUSD Board site.

title: Banned Books Week
location: CA
description:
Banned Books Week was launched in 1982 in response to a sudden surge in the number of challenges to books in libraries, bookstores, and schools. Held in the last week of September or first week of October, the annual event highlights the value of free and open access to information and brings together the entire book community — librarians, educators, authors, publishers, booksellers, and readers of all types — in shared support of the freedom to seek and to express ideas. 
The next Banned Books Week will be held October 4–10, 2026. The theme of this year’s event is: Let Books Be — Protect the Freedom to Read.

title: Davis Neighbors' Night Out
location: CA
description:
Join the City of Davis, Yolo County, ASUCD, and UC Davis in celebrating community during Davis Neighbors’ Night Out. Davis Neighbors’ Night Out is a celebration of our community and a great opportunity for neighbors to get to know one another. Connected neighborhoods create safer and more caring places to live 
  
Events include potlucks, neighborhood games and activities and gatherings of neighbors to meet in the street for good conversation. 
  
Davis Neighbors’ Night Out is open to all ages and is free to participate in. 
  
Neighbors, neighborhood associations, apartment complexes, etc., are encouraged to be an “Event Sponsor.” If you’re interested in becoming an event sponsor, visit: https://www.cityofdavis.org/city-hall/city-manager-s-office/community-events/davis-neighbors-night-out

title: Blood on the Clocktower at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
The first Wednesday of every month, we play _Blood on the Clocktower_, a social deduction game in the vein of Werewolf/Mafia/The Resistance, with a few twists!

We'll have a circle of chairs reserved inside Blue Note, near the back, with a Yolo County Board Game Gathering sign on the table. Just say hello, and we'll show you some games, pull some players together, and get to having fun!

We also usually have a few tables of players playing other board games, if social deduction isn't your bag!

Get a feel for Blood on the Clocktower here: https://youtu.be/4sfa8_kNxsQ
source: Meetup Yolo County Board Game Gathering

title: Healing Arts 6-Session Workshop
description:
Pence Adult Art Programs
The Pence’s 6-session Healing Arts workshop uses art as a healing language for those experiencing grief from the loss of a loved one. Through the process of art making, participants will have opportunities for discussion, education, and connecting with peers in a safe and supportive space in the Pence Learning Center under the guidance of facilitators Amy Vidra and Lyndsey Rocca.

REGISTRATION ONLINE IS REQUIRED IN ADVANCE through the Pence Gallery's website, and space is limited to the first 8 participants who register. Participants must be 18 or older, and no art experience is necessary. This program is generously sponsored by Bob & Joanne Andresen.

Healing Arts 6-Session Workshop
Fridays\, 10\-11:45 AM \| Oct\. 9\, 16\, 23\, 30 & Nov\. 6\, 13
$25 Members, $35 Non-Members (all materials included)

**Reminder - an RSVP on Meetup does NOT count as registration. Registration is required in advance through the [Pence’s website (CLICK HERE)](https://pencegallery.org/education/programs/workshops-and-classes/).**

\*Please note that when registering for this program, you are signing up for all 6 sessions. If you are unable to attend one or more of the sessions, please let us know in advance.

Any questions? Email pencegallery@gmail.com.

The Project













Studio Creatch proudly announces a new theatrical commission inspired by the life of Basil Campbell, a 19th-century pioneer who rose from enslavement to become the wealthiest Black landowner in Superior California. Written by acclaimed Sacramento-based director-playwright Anthony D’Juan, Superior California is a work of historical fiction inspired by the life of Mr. Campbell, bringing to light a powerful, lesser-known chapter of regional history. 




Dates/Times: October 10th & 11th at 7pm 



Admission: Admission is free to the public. Limited seating is available so early arrival is encouraged. 
Content Advisory: Recommended for ages 16+. This production is set in the 19th century and deals directly with the historical realities, and institutional trauma of chattel slavery. In an effort to maintain historical accuracy and dramatic honesty, the script includes some period-accurate racial slurs, offensive terminology, and racially tense dialogue. 
We recognize that these themes and language can be distressing. Prior to the performance we will point out designated exits/quiet spaces for audience members, should they feel the need to step away amidst the performance.

title: Imagining America National Gathering
location: CA
description:
Join over 500 participants from the IA network and the University of California, Davis and Yolo Bioregion community (a geographic and cultural area that includes the cities of Davis, Woodland, Winters, West Sacramento, and surrounding areas) to engage in deep learning, collaboration, and transformative creativity on the theme of Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times. We will activate spaces across the UC Davis campus, in the City of Davis, and at community-hosted site visits. 
Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times calls us to re-story and honor the places, knowledges, relationships, and ecologies that have been made broken through centuries of violence and abandonment, and the current intensifying fear and repression. We know that our communities are tired, and we know that being together revives our collective spirit, giving us the strength and inspiration we need in troubled times. In this moment of upheaval, the 2026 IA National Gathering draws participants to Davis, CA in the spirit of mending the roots of our connections, and to “awaken,” as Buddhist monk and activist Thích Nhất Hạnh teaches, “from the illusion of our separateness.”

title: Voting from Different Perspectives: Studying Elections across Disciplines
location: Virtual
description:

This panel brings together faculty from across UC Davis and UC Davis Health discuss their research on voting and elections within and between different disciplines as well as national and international contexts. Panelists will include: 

Vikram D. Amar, Daniel J. Dykstra Distinguished Professor of Law
Ruth Shim, Director of Cultural Psychiatry and Luke & Grace Kim Professor in Cultural Psychiatry, Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences
Lauren Young, Associate Professor and Director of Graduate Studies, Political Science
Megan Macklin (moderator), Director of Campus Climate and Inclusion Initiatives, Office of Campus and Community Relations/Inclusive Excellence

You must register in advance for this event.

description:
Join us on November 7 at International House Davis for I-Fest 2026, our International Festival Davis! 
For one day, we open our doors wide to celebrate and uplift the many cultures and people who make our region so vibrant. Explore cultural and artisan booths throughout I-House, enjoy food trucks out front, and experience a full lineup of performances on our backyard stage. It’s an open house in the truest sense: for the day, this is your house too, and every culture and community has a place here. 
I-Fest is a celebration, but your participation also supports the work I-House does all year long: welcoming newcomers, supporting English learners, and helping people from around the world find connection and community in Davis. At a time when many of us are feeling anxious or disconnected, creating spaces for joy, belonging, and connection feels more important than ever. Come celebrate cultures, meet new people, share in the joy, and experience what makes our community so special. 
For one day, I-House is your house. Come be part of it.

title: Principles of Community Celebration
location: UC Davis ARC, 760 Orchard Road, Davis, CA, 95616
description:
The 2026 Principles of Community Celebration recognizes the people and partnerships that bring our values to life across UC Davis. 
The celebration will feature recognition of the Soaring to New Heights and ASUCD awards honorees, stories from faculty, staff and students, showcases highlighting community-engaged research and partnerships, and opportunities to connect with colleagues and community partners. 
  
We honor our collective decision to be part of this community, and we celebrate the ongoing work of making UC Davis a place people want to be. 
For more information, visit: https://excellence.ucdavis.edu/events/principles-community-celebration.

title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.
source: Meetup Yolo County Board Game Gathering

title: Davis City Council Meetings
location: City Hall Community Chambers, 23 Russell Blvd, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change. 
  
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance. 
  
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.

title: Human Relations Commission Meetings
location: City Hall Community Chambers, 23 Russell Blvd, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July). 
  
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site. 
  
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council. 
  
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org

title: Blood on the Clocktower at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
The first Wednesday of every month, we play _Blood on the Clocktower_, a social deduction game in the vein of Werewolf/Mafia/The Resistance, with a few twists!

We'll have a circle of chairs reserved inside Blue Note, near the back, with a Yolo County Board Game Gathering sign on the table. Just say hello, and we'll show you some games, pull some players together, and get to having fun!

We also usually have a few tables of players playing other board games, if social deduction isn't your bag!

Get a feel for Blood on the Clocktower here: https://youtu.be/4sfa8_kNxsQ
source: Meetup Yolo County Board Game Gathering
